title: Projects: Workspaces with Knowledge, Instructions, and Memory

questions.prompt: How many projects can a Free user create?
questions.explanation: Projects are available to everyone, and the Help Center says free users can create a maximum of five.

questions.prompt: What does a project give Claude? Select all that apply.

options.text: A knowledge base of your files
Access to every other project's memory

questions.explanation: A project bundles knowledge, instructions, and its own memory. It never uses other projects' memories.

questions.prompt: On paid plans, when a project's knowledge nears the context limit, Claude switches to ____ mode, expanding capacity up to 10x.
questions.explanation: RAG uses a project knowledge search tool to retrieve relevant passages instead of loading everything at once.

questions.prompt: Why do projects help with usage limits?

options.text: Project content is cached and counts less against your limits when reused
Projects don't count toward usage at all
Projects always use the smallest model
Projects compress your files to save tokens

questions.explanation: Per the Help Center, content in projects is cached and counts less against your limits when reused (caches expire after inactivity).

questions.prompt: Order the steps for setting up a useful project.

items.text: Create the project for one focused area of work
Ask questions that name the source document

questions.explanation: Create a focused project, add current well-named files up front, write durable instructions, then ask questions that name specific documents.

questions.prompt: Match each project sharing permission (Team/Enterprise) to what it allows.

pairs.right: See contents and chat in the project
Change instructions and knowledge, manage members
Turn project sharing off for the organization

questions.explanation: Can view lets members use the project; Can edit lets them change it and manage members; owners can disable sharing.
